title: Error Handling
summary: Catch problems with try/except instead of letting your program crash.

checkpoints.title: try, except, and what can go wrong
checkpoints.content: Code inside a `try:` block runs normally, but if it raises an exception, Python jumps straight to a matching `except:` block instead of crashing the program. `except ValueError:` only catches ValueErrors — a different exception type still propagates and crashes, which is usually what you want so real bugs aren't hidden.
checkpoints.explanation: Catching only the specific exceptions you expect (not a bare `except:`) keeps error handling honest — you handle what you anticipated and let genuine bugs surface.

hints.H0: try/except lets you recover from an expected failure instead of crashing.
hints.H1: The except clause only catches the exception type it names.
hints.H2: A bare `except:` catches everything, which usually hides real bugs — prefer naming the exception type.

checkpoints.title: Predict a caught ZeroDivisionError
checkpoints.content: What happens when this runs? `try: 1 / 0` then `except ZeroDivisionError: print("caught it")`

options.text: It prints "caught it" and the program keeps running normally.
options.explanation: 1 / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, which the except clause catches by name, so the print runs and execution continues.

options.text: It crashes with an unhandled ZeroDivisionError.
options.explanation: It doesn't crash — the except clause specifically names ZeroDivisionError, so it's caught, not left unhandled.

options.text: Nothing is printed — the error is silently swallowed.
options.explanation: The except block explicitly runs print("caught it") — catching an exception doesn't mean staying silent.

checkpoints.explanation: Naming the exact exception type lets Python match the error, run the except block, and continue past the try/except normally.

hints.H0: Dividing by zero raises a specific, well-known exception type.
hints.H1: The except clause names that exact type, so it matches.

checkpoints.title: Catch a specific exception
checkpoints.content: After `try: age = int(user_input)`, what except clause catches invalid text and prints "not a number"?
checkpoints.explanation: int() raises ValueError when given text that can't be parsed as a number, so that's the exception type to name.

hints.H0: You need an except clause naming a specific exception type.
hints.H1: Converting invalid text with int() raises a specific, well-known exception.

checkpoints.title: Predict finally's behavior
checkpoints.content: A `try` block has a matching `except` and also a `finally:` block. If no exception is raised at all, does the code in `finally:` still run?

options.text: Yes — finally always runs, whether or not an exception occurred.
options.explanation: finally is guaranteed to run after the try block, regardless of whether an exception was raised or caught — it's for cleanup that must always happen.

options.text: No — finally only runs if an exception was actually caught.
options.explanation: finally runs unconditionally — its whole purpose is guaranteed cleanup, with or without an exception.

options.text: It raises a SyntaxError to have finally without an exception occurring.
options.explanation: There's nothing invalid about this — finally is designed to run in every case, exception or not.

checkpoints.explanation: finally runs no matter what — whether the try block succeeds, raises a caught exception, or raises an uncaught one — making it the right place for cleanup like closing a file.

hints.H0: finally exists specifically for code that must always run.
hints.H1: Its behavior doesn't depend on whether an exception happened.
